Title Electromagnetic Fields from Three Viewpoints
Author(s) Domina Eberle Spencer , Uma Y Shama , Philip J Mann
Keywords Electric Field
Published 1998
Abstract
The field of a static charge distribution will be examined from three viewpoints: the Weber equation, the classical equation on which special relativity is based and the new Gaussian equation. It will be shown that with the Weber equation the force is a function of both velocity and acceleration and with the new Gaussian equation the force in a uniform electric field depends on the velocity of the test charge. But with the classical equation the force is independent of the velocity of the test charge. Experimental trajectories require mass to vary with velocity if the classical equation is postulated as in special relativity. But these trajectories may be consistent with a constant mass in both the Weber and the new Gaussian formulations. The field of a stationary current element is also examined from the three viewpoints. Extra terms occur with the Weber and the New Gaussian equations that will be significant in the analysis of high-speed charges moving in magnetic fields. Finally the force between stationary current elements is analyzed. According to classical theory the force is always perpendicular to the current element on which it acts. Tangential forces such as have been observed in many experiments can occur with both the Weber and the New Gaussian Equations. Aka "The Uniform Electric Field from Three Viewpoints"

title: Electromagnetic Induction and Motor Action across Field-Free Regions

Title Electromagnetic Induction and Motor Action across Field-Free Regions
Author(s) Francisco J Müller
Keywords electromagnetic, action, magnetic field, Voltage
Published 2007
Journal Proceedings of the NPA
Volume 4
Number 2
Pages 175-179
Abstract
It is well known that if a wire of length L moves with a velocity v perpendicularly to a magnetic field B, a voltage is induced along the wire equal to BvL. Reciprocally, if a current I is passed through the wire, a motor force F = BIL tends to move the wire in a perpendicular direction. What is less well known is the case in which the wire is shielded from the magnetic field, for example, inserting it in a coaxial iron cylinder. Inside the shield B = 0. Yet, experiments to be described in this paper show that the same voltage BvL appears on the wire, in spite of the zero B where the wire is located. Likewise, upon passing a current through the shielded wire a motor force is still produced, but this time not on the wire, but on the shielding cylinder. On both instances, the induction and the motor force, are occuring across a field free region. The theoretical perplexities entailed by this ?non-local' phenomena, acting at a distance, are discussed.

The foundations of physics must be continuosly re-examined. Not only the physical theories, but also the very basic notions and entities undergo changes. Warfield's aim is a device that accelerates itself using only a battery, a magnet and a wire — no exhaust, no reaction mass. The paper is entirely a design study; no device is built and no measurement is reported.
The physical claim is a comparison of two forces. In a homopolar motor the current crosses the magnet's field at right angles and inside the magnet, where the field is strongest, so the Lorentz force on it is at a maximum. The return current in the closing wire also sits in the magnet's field, but out where the field is weak and, for much of its path, running parallel to the field lines, where it feels nothing at all. If the closing wire is routed so as to follow the curving field lines for as long as possible before turning back to the battery, the opposing force on it can be made much smaller than the driving force on the disc. What is left over, Warfield argues, is an uncompensated force on the apparatus as a whole — "a violation of Newton's Third Law ". A mirror-symmetric arrangement of two magnets and two closing wires on a fixed platform is then offered to cancel the rotations and lateral components and leave pure translation.

O'Sullivan argues that space is built from two types of energy. The first is finite energy — energy that is bound up with time. In his scheme this is mass-energy, tied to light and gravity and generated by "open-ended standing waves." Finite energy is held to expand as mass in the electric field, while light and gravity act in the magnetic field; gravitational forces located at the anti-nodes of the magnetic field are what shape the mass-energy waves in the electric field, always at the constant speed of light. Photons, in this picture, are the particle aspect of the magnetic-field waves, carrying energy according to Planck's relation E = hf .
The second is infinite energy — energy without time. O'Sullivan defines infinity as energy that has no beginning and no end, toward which the open-ended standing waves are always moving as they approach static equilibrium. The speed of light is presented as the common constant linking the finite and the infinite. The central conclusion is that time does not exist outside of finite energy : time is simply the transfer of finite energy, so where there is no finite energy there is no time.

This Natural Philosophy wiki page disputes content found on Wikipedia page wikipedia:Electromagnetism
Electromagnetism is the study of electricity, magnetism and their connection with light. In its standard modern form it is expressed by Maxwell's equations as reformulated by Oliver Heaviside, together with the Lorentz force law, and it is generally regarded as the most successful and best-tested theory in physics.
The literature collected on this wiki does not dispute that the standard formulation works. It disputes that it is complete, that it is correctly founded, and in several cases that it describes what is physically happening at all. The objections are not variations on a single theme: they come from different directions and are not always compatible with one another. What they share is the conviction that electromagnetism was settled prematurely — that between about 1820 and 1890 a set of live alternatives was narrowed to one, and that the discarded options were dropped for reasons of mathematical convenience rather than experimental refutation.
This article sets out the standard account briefly, then the principal lines of objection found in the papers archived here, then the disagreements among the objectors themselves.
The standard account
On the received view, electric and magnetic fields are physical entities that fill space and carry energy and momentum. Charges create fields; fields propagate at the speed of light; fields exert forces on charges through the Lorentz force F = q ( E + v × B ). Maxwell's displacement current term makes the equations consistent with charge conservation and yields wave solutions travelling at c , identifying light as an electromagnetic wave. Because the theory is Lorentz-invariant it required no revision when special relativity arrived; instead it became relativity's model.

The book presents Catt's unconventional approach to electromagnetic theory, built around the idea of the "energy current" — a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) step of electric and magnetic field that travels at the speed of light in the dielectric between conductors. From this starting point Catt reinterprets charge, current, and the behaviour of capacitors and transmission lines, and works toward what he called "Theory C" (the "C" for Catt), his proposed replacement for conventional electromagnetic theory. The book also raises the "Catt Question" (or "Catt Anomaly") about how charge on a conductor knows to move as a TEM step passes.
About the author
Ivor Catt (1935–2024) was a British electronics engineer known for pioneering work on high-speed digital interconnection and for a long-running critique of conventional electromagnetic theory. See also his Digital Hardware Design .

Electromagnetism and Relativity , published in 1957, was one of the first to provide an analysis of the probable coupling between EM and inertial fields. Cullwick realized that Maxwell's equations and most existing theories of electrodynamics assume that the mass of an electron is zero. At Maxwell's time this was a reasonable assumption. But it is well known today that electrons have mass, and therefore an inertial momemtum is always associated with an electric current. Cullwick suggested in his analysis that coupling terms between EM and inertia may be very small, but would likely appear sometime in the future as we go to higher current densities. And he was one of the first scientists to predict some of the odd effects which can now seen with superconductors. Cullwick was also one of the first to identify and attempt an analysis of the relativistic paradoxes and unusual effects which occur in a rotating EM field. His work still stands today as one of the only existing efforts to consider the problem of a rotating EM field.

Electromechanical Perpetual Motion is a three-page article by Leslee A Kulba , published in 2010 in issue 48 of the Electric Spacecraft Journal , the journal's final double issue. It is the second part of the ten-part handbook on perpetual motion and its testing that Kulba, the journal's technical editor, contributed to that issue, and it carries the survey begun in " Mechanical Perpetual Motion " into magnets, coils and circuits.
The text of the article has not been recoverable, and this page describes its subject and its place in the series rather than its argument.
The subject
Why the electrical version is the durable one
A wheel of weights can be watched. Its failure is visible in a minute and arguable on paper, which is why the mechanical claims of the last three centuries have mostly died quietly. An electrical machine cannot be watched in the same way. Its input and output are quantities that have to be measured , usually in circuits carrying pulsed, switched or reactive waveforms, and the measurement is genuinely difficult — difficult enough that an honest experimenter with ordinary instruments can obtain a reading greater than unity and have no idea why.
That is the reason the series is shaped as it is. Having described the machines in this article, Kulba spends the remaining seven on efficiency, experimental design, instruments, low-level signals, microwave power, power calculation and error analysis. The electrical perpetual motion claim is not refuted by argument in the way the overbalanced wheel is; it is refuted by measuring properly, and most of the handbook is about how.

title: Natural Philosophy Wiki

The electron is the lightest stable electrically charged particle known, discovered by J. J. Thomson at the end of the nineteenth century and the carrier of electric current, of chemical bonding and of most of what is ordinarily called electricity. In mainstream physics it is a structureless point: a lepton of the Standard Model, an excitation of a quantum field, with charge −e, spin ½, a magnetic moment slightly larger than the Dirac value (the "anomalous" moment), and no measured size — scattering experiments are read as placing an upper bound on its radius rather than as revealing a shape. Its behaviour is described by the Dirac equation and by quantum electrodynamics, and its apparent wave properties are treated as intrinsic to a wave-particle duality that is not further analysed.
The literature collected on this wiki disputes almost every part of that description, and it does so with unusual persistence: the electron is one of the most heavily worked topics in the archive. The common complaint is not that quantum electrodynamics computes badly — its numerical success is generally conceded — but that a point particle with a finite charge, a finite spin and a finite magnetic moment is not a physical object at all. A point has no volume in which to store energy, no radius about which to spin, and no current loop with which to generate a magnetic moment; the classical self-energy of a point charge is infinite, and the infinity is removed by renormalisation rather than by explanation. Einstein's remark, quoted repeatedly in these papers — "I would just like to know what an electron is" — serves as the standing motto of the whole enterprise.

Abstract
A mathematical model (the Schrödinger Equation) and a physical model (Spinning Charged Ring Model) of the electron are compared for their ability to predict waves emitted by electrons. Although it is a fundamental postulate of Quantum Mechanics, the Schrödinger Equation does not allow for an interpretation of wave-functions as physical waves, cannot be a complete theoretical description of a micro physical system, neglects intrinsic characteristics of particle motion, and fails in several other ways to correspond to physical reality. The Ring Model of Electrons makes accurate and complete predictions of fields and waves by using the locations and internal motions of charge elements that make up the electron in order to determine the external fields of the electron. The physical Ring Model, compliant with the law of cause and effect, explains the meaning of Planck's Constant and accurately predicts the Photoelectric Effect, wavelengths of hydrogen line spectra, blackbody radiation, and the Compton Wavelength. An unbiased assessment of these facts implies that electrons are small physical particles that closely resemble the Spinning Charged Ring Model, and these electrons are a source of electromagnetic waves.

This paper proposes an experiment intended for showing that the magnetic field of electrons is not the result of their translation, but of their magnetic moment. The magnetic moments of electrons are aligned in the metal cathode until the electrons are ejected towards the anode, and then they pass through the hole provided for this purpose to form a cathodic beam. Electric fields do not change the orientation of the magnetic moments of the electrons. If this beam is deflected up to 90° by an electric field, the magnetic moments of electrons are no longer parallel to their direction of translation, thus the magnetic field of the cathodic beam should disappear or at least no longer be measured by coils placed in a plane containing the beam, unlike what can be observed before deflection.

This short 2014 paper — bylined in the PDF to Jean de Climont , dated May 2014, and given in French as well as English — is not a theoretical derivation but a proposal for a single decisive bench experiment. Its target is one of the foundational identifications of classical electrodynamics: that the magnetic field surrounding a current is produced by the translation of charge.
The author's objection is one of causal economy rather than of measurement. Electrons in a conductor, or in a cathode-ray beam, have two candidate causes of magnetic field available to them at once: their translation speed, and their own intrinsic magnetic moment, which is already held responsible for all the magnetic properties of matter. title: Electron in the Ground Energy State
content_preview:
Title Electron in the Ground Energy State – Part 1
Read in full Link to paper (Internet Archive)
Author(s) David L Bergman , Dennis P Allen
Keywords electron , Potential Energy, magnetic moment
Published 2012
Journal Foundations of Science
Volume 15
Number 1
No. of pages 16
Read the full paper here (archived copy — the original link is no longer available)
Abstract
The structure and internal motions of ground-state electrons are obtained from a physical Spinning Charged Ring (SCR) model. This new electrodynamical model accurately yields the fundamental and structural properties of the electron, including the exact distribution of charge density inside the ring. Equilibrium of charge distributed throughout the ring interior is a result of electromagnetic self-forces that control the structure and internal motions of charge. The model yields the electron rest-mass energy and the electron-positron annihilation energy with energies 510,999 electron-Volts. The model also yields the actual, non-anomalous radius and non-anomalous magnetic moment of the electron. The model predicts the gyromagnetic ratio of a free electron. A current issue in physics is resolved – how "potential energy internal to a particle system come[s] into the picture" – by treating the electron as a system of potential energies and real mass-energies.

The second half of a two-part paper by David L Bergman and Dennis P Allen , published by Common Sense Science in Foundations of Science in 2012. Where Electron in the Ground Energy State – Part 1 establishes the Spinning Charged Ring (SCR) model of the electron and the balance of forces that holds it together, Part 2 solves for the distribution of charge inside the ring and derives the ring's dimensions and magnetic moment from it.
Abstract
Equilibrium of charge distributed throughout the electron ring interior is a result of electromagnetic self-forces that control the structure and internal motion of charge. The exact distribution of charge density inside the ring-shaped electron is described by equations and graphs. The dimensions of ground-state electrons are obtained from a physical spinning charged ring (SCR) model. The model yields the large radius and small radius of the electron ring. And the model also yields the actual non-anomalous magnetic moment of the electron. Thus, the SCR Model predicts that the diameter of a free electron is finite and physically related to electron properties such as its rest-mass, spin, magnetic moment, line spectra, and wavelength.
The model and the stability problem
The paper opens with a thought experiment: work is done to assemble a ring out of the substance the authors call electrical charge, the assembly being carried out slowly so that magnetic induction and radiation do not enter the energy accounting. That work then resides in the ring and its surrounding field as rest-mass or self-energy — on this model the origin of mass is electromagnetic field energy

Establishment physics admires Einstein's GRT gravity theory because of its perceived great mathematical Riemannian 4-dimensional geometry and its curved space time beauties, but does this religion of mathematical beauty coincide with the physical truth of experimental gravity? No, because it's based upon the assumption that gravitational and inertial masses are the same ... or at least always equal, but Russian Professor Alexander L. Dmitriev has done a number of experiments showing that horizontally (fast) spinning rotors do not usually fall with the usual local gravitational acceleration. Furthermore, Morton F. Spears has given a model of gravity that involves spherical capacitors modeling both electrons & protons which tends to explain why Newton's gravitational constant G cannot be calculated accurately to more than 5 significant figures (i.e. due to the local permittivity {or dielectric constant} then being a hidden variable in Newton's theory).

Abstract
In earlier articles of this series, electrostatic repulsion has been associated with fine-grained centrifugal pressure in the linearly polarized electron-positron sea. Magnetic repulsion has also been associated with fine-grained centrifugal pressure in the magnetized electron-positron sea. There is however a major difference between the two cases. An increase in magnetization results in an increase in vorticity H , whereas an increase in linear polarization does not result in an increase in vorticity H . This article takes a closer look at the linear polarization mechanism for rotating electron-positron dipoles and concludes that the internal opposing force involves a centrifugal aether pressure that is induced as a result of the electrons and the positrons coming closer together on average, along the line of action.

Frederick David Tombe's eight-page paper, written in Belfast in July 2008 and amended in Leyte that December, belongs to a long series developing a mechanical aether in the tradition of Maxwell's molecular vortices. It appeared in the General Science Journal .

Within this framework, earlier papers in the series had attributed both electrostatic and magnetic repulsion to "fine-grained centrifugal pressure" in the sea. The present paper addresses an asymmetry between the two cases: magnetising the sea increases its vorticity H , whereas linearly polarising it does not, so a mechanism is needed that raises the centrifugal pressure without raising either the vorticity or the rotational kinetic energy.

Elementary Antigravity is a 1989 book by the engineer Frank J Znidarsic , published by Vantage Press.
Overview
The book is an early statement of Znidarsic's Quantum Transition Theory (later called "Z-Theory"), which uses a classical approach to address quantum puzzles (Planck's constant, quantum jumps, photon energies). Central to it is a characteristic velocity — about 1.09 million metres per second, which Znidarsic identifies with the "speed of sound" within the nucleus — that governs the transition of quantum states. He argues that this framework accounts for cold fusion / LENR and for antigravity as effects of an amplified magnetic component of the strong and gravitational forces. A follow-up, Elementary Antigravity II , continues the theme.
About the author
Frank J. Znidarsic is a registered professional electrical engineer in Pennsylvania who has developed the "Z-Theory" of the quantum transition and written on energy, cold fusion, and antigravity.

A note on the source. This entry is a PowerPoint file rather than a paper, and it is a short one. Extracting its text yields about 570 distinct words — slide titles, one four-column table, and a page of speaker notes — much of it repeated across the deck. There is no derivation, no reference list and no figure caption that survives extraction. The summary below therefore reconstructs the argument from the numbers, which turn out to be enough: the table can be reverse-engineered exactly, and once it is, the whole scheme is visible.
The claim. Matter emanates from ether, and water is "a changed texture of light". Concretely: the 13.6 eV Rydberg photon is the building block of both the proton and the oxide ion, so a water molecule is an assembly of "millions of photons" clustered about seeds of ether. The seed ether "is what scientists and electricians measure as electric charge, Q ", and the number of such seeds is what chemistry calls the oxidation state.
Fernandes offers electrolysis of water as experimental proof that the ether exists, and the Schwarzschild radius as the size an electron takes when it collapses back into ether — evolution into matter, involution into ether, with mass conserved throughout.

title: Empirical Gap in Newtonian Gravity
content_preview:
Title Empirical Gap in Newtonian Gravity
Read in full Link to paper
Author(s) Richard Benish
Keywords gravity
Published 2008
No. of pages 5
Abstract
For practical and historical reasons, most of what we know about gravity is based on observations made or experiments conducted beyond the surfaces of dominant massive bodies (exterior solution). Here we consider one particular type of interior solution experiment that would not be too diffcult to do, but has never been done.
Overview
Empirical Gap in Newtonian Gravity is a five-page paper by Richard Benish of Eugene, Oregon, dated July 2008 and circulated through his GravitationLab site. It makes a narrower and more careful claim than most papers in this collection, and the claim is largely correct.
Benish observes that a standard undergraduate exercise — drop a test object into an evacuated hole through the diameter of a uniformly dense sphere and it executes simple harmonic motion — is presented in textbook after textbook without any citation of evidence. He notes that Wheeler devotes a ten-page chapter of A Journey Into Gravity and Spacetime to the phenomenon, calling it "boomeranging" and describing it as the easiest doorway to Einstein's concept of gravity as spacetime curvature, yet nowhere discusses whether anyone has seen it happen. Essentially the same prediction follows from general relativity as from Newton.
The point Benish presses is that our empirical knowledge of how bodies move under a mass M is confined to the region outside the mass, R ≤ r < ∞. The interior, 0 ≤ r ≤ R , is "a rather basic and a rather large gap". He is explicit that his purpose "is not to raise doubts about what would happen if the experiment were actually performed", and suggests it be regarded as a demonstration rather than a test — but argues it would be worth doing even so, for completeness and, frankly, for beauty.

title: Natural Philosophy Wiki
content_preview:
caption
Wikipedia Dispute : wikipedia:Energy
This Natural Philosophy wiki page disputes content found on Wikipedia page wikipedia:Energy
Energy is, in orthodox physics, a scalar quantity assigned to a physical system which has the useful property of being conserved: it may change form, but in a closed system the total does not change. It is measured in joules, it is calculated from the configuration and motion of matter, and no experiment has ever isolated it from matter. It is, in short, a number.
Much of the literature collected on this wiki holds that physics has forgotten this. The complaint is not that the quantity is wrongly calculated or that conservation is a bad rule; it is that a bookkeeping term has been quietly promoted into a thing — something that can exist on its own, fill space, travel, and act. Once that step is taken, the argument runs, entities such as "pure energy", the "energy of the vacuum" and dark energy follow as a matter of grammar rather than of evidence.
This article sets out what energy is on the standard account, the objection to its objectification as it is made by researchers documented here, the historical precedent that objection appeals to, and the places where the dispute has practical consequences.
The orthodox account
The point at issue is not controversial, and mainstream physics states it plainly when it is being careful. Energy is defined operationally: kinetic energy is a number computed from mass and speed, potential energy a number computed from position in a field, and the sum is found to be constant. Nothing in the definition requires or supplies a substance.
Richard Feynman put it as directly as anyone, in the Lectures on Physics :
It is important to realize that in physics today, we have no knowledge of what energy is . We do not have a picture that energy comes in little blobs of a definite amount. [...] It is an abstract thing in that it does not tell us the mechanism or the reasons for the various formulas.

title: Energy-Time Uncertainty
content_preview:
Title Energy-Time Uncertainty
Read in full Link to paper
Author(s) Richard Oldani
Keywords uncertainty, energy , time, quantum, action
Published 2010
Journal Proceedings of the NPA
Volume 7
No. of pages 5
Pages 351-353
Abstract
Spontaneous emission is viewed as the continuous absorption of energy by an atomic oscillator followed by quantization during decay. Energy-time uncertainty can then be defined in a manifestly covariant way by establishing space-time boundaries on the action integral of the decay process; where the minimum of action is not zero, but h. First order equations are derived describing the emission of a photon. Second order emission is shown to yield the Feigenbaum equation. The similarities between them are noted. It is concluded that discrete forms of time, or oscillation periods, function as operators in Lagrangian quantum mechanics because they take as their inputs a delocalized superposition state and return as their outputs a localized quantum state. It is hypothesized that period doubling must be accompanied by asymmetric geometries.
Overview
Energy-Time Uncertainty is a five-page paper by Richard Oldani , presented at the 17th conference of the Natural Philosophy Alliance and published in the Proceedings of the NPA volume 7 (2010), pages 351–353.
Its starting complaint is that special relativity requires symmetry between the space and time parameters, and that quantum mechanics "lacks an energy-time uncertainty relation" of the same character as Δ x Δ p ≥ ħ/2. Title Energy Impulse Secrets
Read in full Link to paper
Author(s) Philipp M Kanarev
Published 2010
No. of pages 9
Abstract
Energy impulses keep preserving their secrets. The errors in Newton's dynamics and electrodynamics are the main causes of incomprehension of these secrets. A recovery of these errors will open new energy possibilities before mankind; these possibilities will rescue mankind from an environmental disaster, which is generated by hydrocarbon energy sources. It is not a naked forecast. Its authenticity is proved both theoretically and experimentally.
Overview
Philipp Kanarev, Professor Emeritus of Physics at Krasnodar, argues that Newtonian dynamics contains errors that have concealed the true nature of impulsive forces, and that correcting them opens "new energy possibilities before mankind" capable of rescuing us from the environmental consequences of hydrocarbon fuels.
The paper has three parts. First, a critique of the textbook treatment of impulse and impact force, addressed throughout to "dear mathematicians" whose symphonic derivations, he says, leave engineers without any way to compute the quantities that matter. Second, an application to a real disaster: the destruction of turbine unit 2 at the Sayano-Shushenskaya hydroelectric station in August 2009, in which a 2,580-tonne assembly was thrown fourteen metres into the turbine hall and 75 people died. Third, a proposed explanation of that event in terms of pressure exerted by infrared photons released when water clusters re-form, and a pulsed electrical generator said to exploit the same principle.
Kanarev's alternative framework, which he calls mechanodynamics, adds an "inertial force" F i = mb i to the list of forces resisting motion, and defines impact force as the change of momentum divided by the time over which it changes.

title: Energy Loss by Electrons in an Absorber
content_preview:
Title Energy Loss by Electrons in an Absorber
Read in full Read in full
Author(s) Ricardo L Carezani
Keywords Autodynamics , inelastic scattering, Bethe-Heitler theory, Neutrino, beta rays, heavy nuclei
Published Society for the Advancement of Autodynamics (unpublished)
Website https://www.autodynamics.org/energy-loss-by-electrons-in-absorber/
"Energy Loss by Electrons in Absorber" is an unpublished paper by Ricardo L Carezani applying the Autodynamics equations to a discrepancy in the pre-war scattering literature: measurements of the energy lost by fast electrons traversing absorbers of heavy nuclei that came out well above the Bethe–Heitler prediction. It is the one Autodynamics paper that engages a quantitative anomaly in a regime where the neutrino had already been experimentally excluded.
Abstract
For many years a considerable number of experimenters have reported that the energy loss by electrons traversing absorbers of heavy nuclei is larger than the energy calculated from the well-established Bethe-Heitler theory considering together energy loss by collision and radiation. This is particularly true when only the radiation is considered. The phenomenon is far from an explanation accounting for the electrons stopped by the absorber. To account for the excess of energy loss, many authors suggested the emission of neutrinos, but as was overwhelming proved experimentally by Buechner and van de Graaff there was no energy carried away by neutrinos or other penetrating radiation. For the first time, this phenomenon is explained by a general theory.
Overview
Carezani's historical framing is the strongest part of the paper. Between roughly 1915 and 1956, cloud-chamber experiments on beta rays between 0.5 and 17 MeV repeatedly found inelastic scattering in heavy elements several times the Bethe–Heitler value — factors of 2 to 5 in krypton and xenon, 10 in argon, 30 in lead, 6 in mercury. content_preview:
Title Energy Storage in Inductors and Ampère's Law
Read in full Link to paper
Author(s) James Keele
Keywords Ampere's Law, Inductance, SRT
Published 2003
Journal Galilean Electrodynamics
Volume 14
Number 4
No. of pages 5
Pages 78
Abstract
This paper shows that the potential energy set up by the Ampère force between current elements is the mechanism for energy storage in inductors. The use of Ampère's Law , without reference to a 'magnetic field', explains energy storage in the simple inductors experimented tested and reported upon in this paper. The paper shows how to develop a computer model for a one-turn inductor and calculate the energy stored in the inductor.

title: Energy Stored in a Gravitational Field
content_preview:
Title Energy Stored in a Gravitational Field
Author(s) Mahmoud A Melehy
Keywords gravitational field, energy , magnetic field
Published 2001
Abstract
It is well known that there is energy stored in any space penetrated by an electric, or a magnetic field. This paper, however, shows that there is, likewise, energy stored in any space penetrated by a gravitational field. By a non-relativistic method, we calculate the energy stored, wg, in a planetary gravitational field, per unit volume. Near the surface of Planet Earth, the result shows that wg is approximately 15.9 Megawatt-hour/cubic-meter. How much of this enormous amount of energy can be extracted is a difficult question to answer.

title: Energy Transformation and Flow; A Theory of Evolution
content_preview:
Title Energy Transformation and Flow; A Theory of Evolution
Read in full Link to paper
Author(s) Richard Oldani
Keywords thermodynamics, evolution, spontaneous emission
Published 2006
Journal Physics Essays
Volume 19
Number 4
No. of pages 11
Abstract
Spontaneous emission by an atomic oscillator is defined in terms of energy transformation and flow. The description is expanded to include dissipative systems by introducing energy equipartition as a property of the flow. The Feigenbaum constant is derived quantum mechanically. A law of flow equivalent to the laws of thermodynamics is formulated for bounded systems and is then applied to living organisms. The common genetic structure of cells is seen as fulfilling the structural requirement of equipartition while the tendency of the organism towards an equilibrium state, or homeostasis, describes the equipartitioned flow. Since energy flow increases by superposition evolution may be interpreted as an extended series of spontaneous energy transformations from external to internal modes. Finally evolutionary theory is used heuristically to define a universal law of energy flow and to introduce time as a quantum mechanical variable. Two experimental tests are proposed.
Overview
Richard Oldani's paper is an attempt to run a single explanatory scheme from the atom to the fossil record. Its organising move is a change of coordinates: instead of describing physical systems in the canonical position–momentum pair ( q , p ), Oldani proposes to describe them in the energy–time pair ( E , t ), on the ground that "energy flow" is a variable common to an atomic oscillator, a convecting fluid, a neuron and a species. Once that substitution is made, he argues, the material structures supporting the flow "can for practical purposes be ignored", and phenomena that look unrelated turn out to have the same shape.

Energy Unlimited was an American magazine on unconventional energy published by Walter P. Baumgartner of Albuquerque, New Mexico, between 1978 and 1987. Its subjects were magnetism, water and vortex phenomena, and the cosmologies of Viktor Schauberger and Walter Russell , on both of whom Baumgartner wrote and lectured.
History
The magazine began in 1978 as a quarterly, with four issues that year, and continued at that rate into the early 1980s before becoming irregular: issues 17 and 18 were published together as a single number for spring and summer 1984, and the final three issues appeared one a year in 1985, 1986 and 1987.
Little independent documentation of the magazine has been located beyond the issues themselves and Baumgartner's own later writing. Its circulation, print run and the circumstances of its closure are not recorded in any source consulted here, and nothing is asserted about them.
Holdings in the Aether Physics archive
An offline research archive assembled by John Reed and surveyed in September 2026 holds all 21 numbered issues , 1 to 21, covering the magazine's whole run from January–March 1978 to 1987. Issues 17 and 18 are a single combined number, as published. The documents are not hosted on this wiki.

Author(s) Jeff Yee
Keywords Aether , standing waves, wave centers, Wave Structure of Matter, particle mass, unified force
Year 2014 (first papers); named 2017
Website https://energywavetheory.com
Energy Wave Theory ( EWT ) is a classical wave model of particles and forces developed by Jeff Yee . It treats the universe as a physical medium — an aether — that oscillates to form waves, and holds that everything normally described as a particle, a mass, a charge or a force is a consequence of wave behaviour in that medium, computed with ordinary classical mechanics rather than quantum formalism.
Its two central claims are structural. Matter is standing waves : a particle is a region where travelling longitudinal waves are reflected by wave centers, forming a standing wave of stored energy out to a radius where the amplitude decays back into travelling waves. That radius is the particle's edge, and the stored energy is its mass. Forces are wave interference : the same equation governs the strong, electromagnetic and gravitational forces, which differ only in wave form and amplitude, because particles move to the point of minimal wave amplitude.
Yee's stated ambition is reductive. He argues that the energies of all particles and the strengths of three of the four forces follow from four universal constants and one property of the electron , with no free parameters beyond those five.
Origins
EWT descends from the Wave Structure of Matter tradition. Yee credits three independent sources as leading to his work: Milo M Wolff , whose wave structure of matter modelled the electron as spherical in-waves and out-waves about a wave center; Gabriel LaFreniere , whose wave simulations gave the picture a visual form; and Xavier Borg .

Energy Wave Theory is the YouTube channel of Jeff Yee , on which he presents the model of the same name — a classical account in which the universe is a physical medium, particles are standing waves in it, and the fundamental forces are consequences of wave interference rather than separate interactions.
The channel is compact and explanatory. Some sixty-seven videos published since January 2018 have drawn over half a million views, most of them to a single introductory series.
Content

These are the most-watched items on the channel by a wide margin, and they function as the public entry point to the theory .

David de Hilster will be interviewing Jeff Yee about this new project for modeling his wave energy theory. Jeff is sponsoring a competition held for developers to contribute to the open source project, with prize money awarded to the winning submission in each phase of the project. There are initially five phases to the project, with a total of $15,000 in cash prizes awarded. The dates and requirements for each phase are found in the next section. To simulate the creation of particles, atoms and matter with classical physics, illustrating that the universe operates under a single set of classical laws.
Summary
Jeff Yee presenting not his theory but a project: an open-source contest, funded from his own pocket, to simulate the construction of matter from the smallest particles upward using classical physics alone.
The contest
The stated objective is to simulate the creation of particles, atoms and matter with classical laws, illustrating that the universe operates under a single set of laws — against the present division between the rules for the large and the rules for anything smaller than an atom.
He has broken it into five phases over a year, each about two months, working from the smallest scale up: space-time, particles, nucleons, atoms, molecules. Each phase carries $2,500 for the winner and $500 for a runner-up out of the $15,000 he has committed, with others having offered to add to it. After a two-week judging period the winning code is checked into open source and becomes the starting point for the next phase — because, as he put it, this is like physics: everything should build on what came before.

title: Energy is Everything: Quantum Explanation of Gravity and Inertia
content_preview:
Title Energy is Everything: Quantum Explanation of Gravity and Inertia
Author(s) David W Talmage , Richard J Sanderson
Keywords gravity, inertia, energy , speed of light , gravitational field
Published 2002
Journal Galilean Electrodynamics
Volume 13
Number 6
Pages 115-117
Abstract
This paper argues that the infinities that have plagued previous attempts to quantize gravity can be avoided by changing the causal sequence by which the quantum field produces the attractive force. Instead of acting directly on matter particles, as with electromagnetism, we are proposing that in the case of gravity the quantum field acts indirectly through a change in the speed of light. This difference permits us to use the same explanation for the inverse square laws that characterize both forces, while giving unique explanations for the unique properties of the gravitational field: its relative weakness, its non-absorbability and its ability to produce a change in the clock rate of matter particles and a curvature of light path. At the same time, our proposal that the speed of light controls the energy content of matter particles creates a central role for the isotropic light speed frame. Although this frame cannot be detected, the energy content of matter particles will be affected by their motion relative to this frame. In this way the equivalence of gravity and acceleration, and the requirement for energy exchange to produce the latter, can be explained.

Scientific career

Eric P. Dollard (born 1952) is an American electrical engineer and researcher, and among the very few people credited with successfully reproducing Nikola Tesla 's experiments in wireless power transmission — including, on his supporters' account, the only working Magnifying Transmitter built since Tesla's death. His central contention is that conventional electrical theory contains only half the story, because it treats electricity as a single quantity rather than as two incommensurate components.
His theoretical work links Tesla with Steinmetz, and his broader corpus connects the thought of Tesla, Viktor Schauberger and Wilhelm Reich . Borderland Sciences, which published most of his papers, describes that corpus as among the most important material it has issued.
Education and early career
Dollard's training was practical rather than academic, and unusually early. As a teenager he was given access to RCA's Bolinas radio facility on the northern California coast — then one of the largest radio stations in the United States — for his own investigations into high-frequency alternating current. He worked there from about the age of seventeen, and left high school holding engineering certifications.
Bolinas is the thread running through his work. The Marconi–RCA station there, established around 1913, is the subject of his paper Theory of Wireless Power , which diagrams the installation as it stood about 1919, and of his later book Wireless Giant of the Pacific . When RCA closed the station he was given a large quantity of its electrical equipment, which he subsequently went to considerable lengths to preserve.

Abstract
The paper mentions the essential experimental and theoretical facts which rule out heat as being the driving force of water-arc explosions. The only reasonable explanation of these powerful explosions is the presence in the water of electrodynamic forces. title: Natural Philosophy Wiki
content_preview:
The aether (also spelled ether ) is the name given to a material medium supposed to fill all of space and to serve as the physical carrier of light, of electric and magnetic fields, and in many versions of gravitation and of matter itself. The spelling "aether" is generally preferred on this wiki to distinguish the physical medium from the organic compound of the same name.
For most of the nineteenth century the existence of such a medium was not a fringe position but the central working assumption of physics. Light was known to be a wave, waves were known to be disturbances in something, and the great task of Victorian physics was to determine what that something was made of. James Clerk Maxwell built his electromagnetic theory on a mechanical model of it. After 1905 the mainstream abandoned the medium: Einstein's special relativity showed that the equations could be written without it, and the aether passed out of the physics curriculum, surviving in the textbooks mainly as a cautionary tale about superfluous hypotheses.
It did not pass out of physics altogether. The aether is the single most persistent organising idea in the literature collected on this wiki: Category:Aether holds well over five hundred pages, and the paper archive contains some 373 items on the subject, spanning from the 1970s to the present. The researchers documented here return to it because they regard a field without a medium as an unfinished explanation — a description of what happens rather than an account of how it happens.
What this article cannot do is present "the aether theory," because there is no such thing. The most important fact about the aether literature on this wiki is that it contains many different aethers, and they are not compatible with one another. Some are fluids, some are solids, some are clouds of particles, some are not substances at all but simply preferred reference frames. Ether Occurrence, Part 2 is the 1994 second instalment of Явление эфира — The Phenomenon of the Ether — a four-part monograph issued in Russian at Nikolaev, now Mykolaiv in southern Ukraine, by the physics teacher P D Prussov between 1992 and 1998. It is not a free-standing book but one brochure in a serialised argument: that light, charge, the fields, the elementary particles and the planetary systems are all built out of a single gas-like medium, the ether , and that physics went wrong at the moment it agreed to do without one.
The title used here is the literal rendering carried by the Worldwide List of Dissident Scientists catalogue. Явление in Prussov's title means the manifestation or showing-forth of the ether rather than an occurrence of it; The Phenomenon of the Ether is the closer English title, and is how the work is cited in the Russian-language literature.
The four parts
Prussov, born in 1925 and a lecturer in higher mathematics at the Nikolaev Shipbuilding Institute until his retirement in 1989, began publishing his ether physics only in his late sixties. The four parts appeared, in his own words, на благотворительной основе — on a charitable basis, meaning they were paid for by well-wishers and given away rather than sold through a trade publisher:
Part 1 — Явление эфира . Nikolaev: RIP "Rionika", 1992. 134 pp.
Part 2 — Явление эфира. Часть 2 . Nikolaev, 1994.
Part 3 — Явление эфира. Часть 3 . Nikolaev, 1996.
Part 4 — Явление эфира. Часть 4 . Nikolaev, 1998.
The sequence was then folded into a single volume, Physics of the Ether ( Физика эфира , Nikolaev: Privat-Poligrafiya, 2003, 286 pp.), which Prussov described as the first encyclopedia of the ether and which is the only one of his books to have been digitised.

Abstract
Gravitation might make a preferred frame appear, and with it a clear space/time separation?the latter being, a priori, needed by quantum mechanics (QM) in curved space-time. Several models of gravitation with an ether are discussed: they assume metrical effects in an heterogeneous ether and/or a Lorentz-symmetry breaking. One scalar model, starting from a semi-heuristic view of gravity as a pressure force, is detailed. It has been developed to a complete theory including continuum dynamics, cosmology, and links with electromagnetism and QM. To test the theory, an asymptotic scheme of post-Newtonian approximation has been built. That version of the theory which is discussed here predicts an internal-structure effect, even at the point-particle limit. The same might happen also in general relativity (GR) in some gauges, if one would use a similar scheme. Adjusting the equations of planetary motion on an ephemeris leaves a residual difference with it; one should adjust the equations using primary observations. The same effects on light rays are predicted as with GR, and a similar energy loss applies to binary pulsars.

title: Ether as a Disclosing Model
content_preview:
Title Ether as a Disclosing Model
Author(s) Michael C Duffy

Abstract
The modern ether concept is compatible with relativity, quantum mechanics, and non-classical geometrization. Misuse of the term "ether" in anti-Relativity polemics in former times causes many physicists to avoid the word and equivalent terms are used instead. The modern concept results from three development programmes. First, there was the evolution of Relativity, Relativistic Cosmology and Geometrodynamics which discarded the early 20th C passive, rigid, ether in favour of geometrized space-time. A non-classical ether, defined as field or space-time, was accepted by Einstein in his later years. This had two main aspects: static (or geometric) and dynamic (or frame-space perspective). Second, there was a Lorentzian programme, which provided a quasi-classical exposition of Relativity in terms of moving rod and clock readings. The Einstein-Minkowski and the Lorentzian programmes can be reconciled. The third development programme is associated with Quantum Mechanics and studies of the physical vacuum. A group of analogues based on the vortex sponge promises to unify these programmes of interpretation. The modern ether, from the smallest scale point of view, resembles a "sea of information", which demands new techniques for interpreting it, drawn from information science, computer science, and communications theory.

Abstract
The mysterious ether is discussed regarding transmission of light and gravity. Michelson-Morley's experiments (MMX) are explained.
Overview
Ethereal Ether and Michelson's Mystery is a four-page paper by John-Erik Persson (2011), companion to Dilatory Dilation from the same year and drawing on the same framework.
Its argument is that the ether debate has been posed wrongly. Persson distinguishes an autonomous ether — a preferred frame , as most ether theorists assume — from an entrained ether, a preferred field v(r) determined by the distribution of matter, which he advocates. The autonomous version, he argues, is refuted by planetary motion without retardation, and by the fact that GPS reduces its data in an Earth-centred frame while VLBI uses a Sun-centred one, so that "we use different frames for different heavenly bodies."
The entrained ether is taken to be falling toward each body, which supplies gravity along Le Sage lines. Persson notes the standard difficulty and sets it aside: "Le Sage predicts gravitational shielding, but Newton does not. The effect of gravitational shielding is however very small and experiments to confirm the idea have failed."
The paper's distinctive proposal is its explanation of the Michelson–Morley null result. Atoms in a crystal, he suggests, hold their spacing by exchanging signals through the ether, and those signals suffer the same second-order two-way delay as the light in the interferometer. So the apparatus contracts by exactly the amount needed to cancel the effect being sought:
"The searched effect in light is therefore compensated in the crystal. This explains the hundred years of zero results with MMX, since MMX is useless."

title: Evidence For Weber-Wesley Electrodynamics
content_preview:
Title Evidence For Weber-Wesley Electrodynamics
Author(s) Paul Wesley
Keywords Weber-Wesley electrodynamics, electromagnetic radiation, antenna, velocity
Published 1989
Pages 289-343
Abstract
Weber-Wesley electrodynamics predicts all of the usual results of the Maxwell theory including electromagnetic radiation. It also predicts results where the Maxwell theory fails or is not applicable:
the force on Ampere's bridge in agreement with the measurements of Moyssides and Pappas
the tension required to rupture current carrying wires as observed by Graneau
the force to drive the Graneau-Hering submarine
the force to drive the mercuty in Hering's pump
the zero self-torque observed by Pappas and Vaughan on a Z-shaped antenna
the localized unipolar induction observed by Kennard and Muller
the result of Kaufman's measurement of e/m without mass change with velocity
a nonradiating hydrogen atom, and
the fine-structure splitting of hydrogen-atom energy levels without mass change with velocity.
It is concluded that there is, thus, no evidence supporting mass change with velocity. Experiments are suggested.

title: Evolution of the Plasma Universe: II The Formation of Systems of Galaxies
content_preview:
Title Evolution of the Plasma Universe: II The Formation of Systems of Galaxies
Author(s) Anthony L Peratt
Keywords evolution, universe, plasma, magnetic fields, spiral galaxies
Published 1986
Journal IEEE Transactions on Plasma Science
Volume 14
Number 6
Pages 763-778
Abstract
The model of the plasma universe, inspired by totally unexpected phenomena observed with the advent and application of fully three-dimensional electromagnetic particle-in-cell simulations to filamentary plasmas, consists of studying the interaction between field-aligned current-conducting, galactic-dimensioned plasma sheets or filaments (Birkeland currents). In a preceding paper, the evolution of the interaction spanned some 108-109 years, where simulational analogs of synchrotron-emitting double radio galaxies and quasars were discovered. This paper reports the evolution through the next 109-5 ?? 109 years. In particular, reconfiguration and compression of tenuous cosmic plasma due to the self-consistent magnetic fields from currents conducted through the filaments leads to the formation of elliptical, peculiar, and barred and normal spiral galaxies. The importance of the electromagnetic pinch in producing condense states and initiating gravitational collapse of dusty galactic plasma to stellisimals, then stars, is discussed. Simulation data are directly compared to galaxy morphology types, synchrotron flux, Hi distributions, and fine detail structure in rotational velocity curves. These comparisons suggest that knowledge obtained from laboratory, simulation, and magnetospheric plasmas offers not only to enhance our understanding of the universe, but also to provide feedback information to laboratory plasma experiments from the unprecedented source of plasma data provided by the plasma universe.

Scientific Theory
Name Fourth phase of water
Type Proposed phase of matter / interfacial water model
Author(s) Gerald Pollack
Keywords exclusion zone, EZ water, structured water, H3O2, Nafion, charge separation, infrared, Water
Year 2003 onward
The fourth phase of water — also called EZ water , exclusion-zone water or structured water — is the proposal, advanced by the University of Washington bioengineer Gerald Pollack , that water possesses an ordered, gel-like phase distinct from solid, liquid and vapour. It forms next to hydrophilic (water-loving) surfaces, is negatively charged, and separates charge spontaneously — making it, in Pollack's account, a battery charged by ambient light.
An important distinction should be drawn at the outset. The underlying phenomenon is not in dispute : the exclusion zone has been observed and replicated by at least ten independent laboratories. The exclusion zone
The effect was first observed in Pollack's laboratory in 2003 , next to polyvinyl alcohol gels, and reported on a much larger scale in 2006 next to Nafion , a hydrophilic polymer. Journal Progress In Physics
Volume 2

Read the full paper here (archived copy — the original link is no longer available)
Abstract
Many theoretical papers refer to the need to create exotic materials with average negative energies for the formation of space propulsion anomalies such as "wormholes" and "warp drives". However, little hope is given for the existence of such material to resolve its creation for such use. From the standpoint that non-minimally coupled scalar fields to gravity appear to be the current direction mathematically. It is proposed that exotic material is really scalar field interactions. Within this paper the Ginzburg-Landau (GL) scalar fields associated with superconductor junctions is investigated as a source for negative vacuum energy fluctuations, which could be used to study the interactions among energy fluctuations, cosmological scalar (i. e., Higgs) fields, and gravity.

Overview
This paper proposes an experiment to test space quantization — the quantum-mechanical claim that the component of a free electron 's angular momentum along a magnetic field can take only the values ±ℏ/2, never anything between.
Wagner's objection is stated as a matter of physical intuition rather than of formalism. Quantum theory's statistical predictions work, but he supposes there must be a causal story underneath them, and offers the Galton board as his model of what such a story looks like: thousands of beads falling through interleaved pegs produce a Gaussian distribution, and nobody concludes from that curve that the beads were in many places at once. Applied to a polarized electron beam, his position is that "polarized" should mean the spin vectors point into the same hemisphere, not that they all share one identical projection.
From that assumption he derives a specific, checkable number . If the spin vectors are distributed over the upper hemisphere rather than fixed at the quantum-mechanical angle, the total angular momentum a polarized beam can deliver along the field direction is about 13.4 per cent less than quantum theory predicts. Published 2011
Journal Proceedings of the NPA
Volume 8
No. of pages 8
Pages 132-139
Abstract
Since at least as early as the 1920's it has been documented within the literature that asymmetric capacitors exhibit a net force in the direction of their charges when high voltages are applied. It also has been demonstrated that certain electrode shapes have an impact on the effectiveness of this effect, that which is called "the Biefield-Brown Effect". The author herein explores the limitations of certain designs in order to better understand the physics of this phenomenon, as well as to add measurable data to this study. Nine designs are considered and strict controls are applied to the experimental steps in order to provide the best possible data and analysis for this research. It has been found through this research that the "skin effect" of a charged metal can give insight into better designs, as well as the electrical breakdown distances of the dielectric materials of such capacitors. While this paper does not rule in (nor out) the exclusivity of ion wind in such designs, it does bring into account where and when such ion wind factors are a critical block to future technologies in this regard, as well as to where and when they are not.

An eight-page experimental report given to the 2011 Natural Philosophy Alliance conference at College Park, Maryland, describing a bench experiment carried out by Jeffrey N Cook at Maumee, Ohio.

It is the second half of the second volume of Experimental Aetherometry , following volume 2A (2004) and preceding volume 3A .
Its central proposal is that there exists a second kind of electricity — massfree or ambipolar — distinct both from ordinary charge flow and from electromagnetic radiation, and that this is what Tesla meant by longitudinal waves and what Reich meant by orgone.
What the book argues
The Correas' claim is that three things previously treated as separate, or as mythology, are one physical phenomenon:
Tesla's longitudinal electricity — what has been variously called Tesla waves, Tesla radiation or Tesla currents
Reich's orgone (OR) and deadly orgone (DOR) — and its reported dual thermal and electroscopic effect on orgone accumulators and Faraday cages
their own ambipolar radiation , or massfree electricity
They argue that Tesla was right that the phenomenon reduces neither to fluxes of monopolar charge nor to electromagnetic radiation, but failed to distinguish it clearly from either; and that Reich failed to give energy and frequency spectra for OR and DOR, or to pin down what his "orgonotic charges" were. The book's claim to originality is that it supplies what both lacked: a spectrum for massfree electric energy, and an account of its interactions.

title: Experimental Concepts for Generating Negative Energy in the Laboratory
content_preview:
Title Experimental Concepts for Generating Negative Energy in the Laboratory
Read in full Link to paper
Author(s) Harold E Puthoff , Eric W Davis
Keywords energy , Theory of Relativity
Published 2006
Pages 1362-1373
Abstract
Implementation of faster-than-light (FTL) interstellar travel via traversable wormholes, warp drives, or other spacetime modification schemes generally requires the engineering of spacetime into very specialized local geometries. The analysis of these via Einstein's General Theory of Relativity (GTR) field equations plus the resultant equations of state demonstrate that such geometries require the use of "exotic" matter in order to induce the requisite FTL spacetime modification. Exotic matter is generally defined by GTR physics to be matter that possesses (renormalized) negative energy density, and this is a very misunderstood and misapplied term by the non-GTR community. We clear up this misconception by defining what negative energy is, where it can be found in nature, and we also review the experimental concepts that have been proposed to generate negative energy in the laboratory.
Overview
This is not a dissident paper. Eric Davis and Harold Puthoff's contribution to the 2006 Space Technology and Applications International Forum is a review of a mainstream topic in general relativity and quantum field theory: what "exotic matter" means, why faster-than-light spacetime geometries require it, and which laboratory effects are known to produce negative energy density.
Its stated purpose is corrective. Negative energy, the authors write, "has the unfortunate reputation of alarming physicists", and the term "exotic matter" is "a very misunderstood and misapplied term by the non-GTR community". Their answer is that the energy conditions which supposedly forbid it were never laws but hypotheses — introduced by Hawking and Ellis in 1973 as working assumptions for singularity theorems — and that they are violated routinely by ordinary quantum systems

title: Experimental Detection of the Ether
content_preview:
Title Experimental Detection of the Ether
Author(s) Wilbur Silvertooth
Keywords luminiferous ether, Michelson-Morley , Kennedy-Thorndike, Special Relativity
Published 1986
Journal Speculations in Science and Technology
Volume 10
Number 1
Pages 3-7
Abstract
This paper revisits the once-important subject of the luminiferous ether, and presents what we believe is a compelling empirical case to reestablish this medium as a viable physical construct. We first review the historical background leading up to the unsuccessful search for ether drift arising from the movement of Earth in its approximately uniform motion around its Sun. Following this, the failure of the Michelson-Morley and Kennedy-Thorndike second-order ether-drift detection experiments is explained by the experimentally established Fitzgerald-Lorentz-Larmour contractions. Two well-known first-order experiments are then presented and it is shown that the associated optical phenomena represent detection of ether drift occurring as a result of the revolving Earth. The analysis of these two experiments is done in the framework of an absolute space, and takes the Fitzgerald-Lorentz-Larmour contractions fully into account. Our results (along with the considerable data that accumulated up to the end of the 19th century) provide direct experimental confirmation of the existence of the luminiferous ether-the great dream of Michelson and Morley - and completely invalidate Einstein's Special Relativity Theory.

The paper reports a measurement. Two flat disc magnets about 6 inches in diameter and ¾ inch thick, magnetised in halves and sintered in hard rubber, were mounted on a non-ferromagnetic stainless steel shaft running on linear ball bearings, with forces and torques read off electronic digital scales. title: Experimental Evidence of 4He Production Cold Fusion Experiment
content_preview:
Title Experimental Evidence of 4He Production Cold Fusion Experiment
Read in full Link to paper (Internet Archive)
Author(s) Antonella De Ninno , Giuliano Preparata
Keywords Cold fusion, Palladium, Helium
Published 2002
Read the full paper here (archived copy — the original link is no longer available)
Abstract
We report the simultaneous production of excess enthalpy and of 4He in a one dimensional Palladium (Pd) stripe cathode electrolytically loaded with Deuterium (D), occurring when the stoichiometric ratio x=[D]/[Pd] exceeds 1. The excess heat is signalled by the local temperature rise, measured by a commercial Peltier element in good thermal contact with the thin film cathode substrate. In order to detect the very small amount of 4He expected in the gas mixture exiting from the cell, we remove effectively all non inert components of the gas mixture (especially hydrogen isotopes) with a non-evaporable getter (NEG) pump. Noble gases remain in the gas phase and they are periodically analysed by the mass spectrometer. The observation of a sizeable transmutation of Deuterium into Helium proves unequivocally that a nuclear transmutation process is the cause of the so called "Cold Fusion". From the amount of Helium, under the assumption of the conversion 2D??4He+23.8 MeV, one can estimate the produced power. We find that such power generally exceeds the one trivially estimated from the temperature rise. This mismatch is increasing with the produced power level and it is well understood by the non equilibrium thermal conditions in the immediate vicinity of the stripe and the consequent leakage of a major fraction of the produced heat by radiation. Indeed, further increasing the produced power, we have induced the actual melting of the thin cathode, proving that one has reached locally a temperature of 1828 K. The phenomenon has been reproduced several times: the quantitative outcomes of Helium in different experiments obviously depend on the level of Deuterium loading

Abstract
While present standard unified field and high energy models require "big science" for experimental verification, a fairly recent theory offers the prospect of allowing experimental investigations at a level that can be performed with more traditional experimental systems. We have performed an experiment based on the dynamic theory of Pharis E. Williams that attempts to search for the existence of a macroscopic coupling between electromagnetism and gravity. Abstract
Atmospheric electricity (AE) refers to the electrical phenomena occurring in the atmosphere of the Earth. There are many manifestations of AE, ranging the spectacular to the subtle. Lightning is one of the most visible phenomena, but AE also probably plays a key role in other major atmospheric disturbances such as tornadoes. The presence of AE can be also be measured even on clear days ("clear air electricity") by means of appropriate detecting devices. Benjamin Franklin and Lord Kelvin were two of the most notable people that studied these effects. Most importantly, it has been reported by quite a few people that AE can be used to power electrostatic motors. These amazing claims of AE derived electromotive power were first made at least one hundred years ago. These claims raise the tantalizing prospect that AE can be a viable source of alternative power. If these reports are true, why has this not already become commonplace in our society? It is the purpose of this paper to report on our preliminary work on verifying the existence of AE in quantities that may someday be sufficient to be a useful source of terrestrial power.

Experimental Studies in Electricity and Magnetism is a collection of the experimental work of the American physicist Francis E Nipher , originally published in 1914 (by P. Blakiston's Son & Co., Philadelphia) and reissued in 2007 by Kessinger Publishing.
Overview
The volume gathers Nipher's laboratory studies in electricity and magnetism, including the experiments that led him to propose an intimate relation between gravitation and electrical action. Nipher argued that the gravitational attraction between two masses depends not only on their masses and separation but also on their electrical condition, and reported experiments which he interpreted as showing that gravitational attraction could be reduced to zero — or even reversed into repulsion — by electrification.
About the author
Francis Eugene Nipher (1847–1926) was an American physicist and long-time professor at Washington University in St. Louis, and a founder of the Academy of Science of St. Louis. He is remembered for his meteorological and magnetic surveys of Missouri and, later in his career, for his controversial electro-gravitational experiments.

content_preview:
Title Experimental Verifications of Isoredshift with Possible Absence of Universe Expansion, Big Bang, Dark Matter, and Dark Energy
Read in full Link to paper
Author(s) Ruggero Maria Santilli
Keywords dark matter , Dark Energy , Big Bang , universe, cosmological redshift
Published 2010
Journal Open Astronomy Journal
Abstract
In this paper, we present systematic studies on the insufficiencies of special relativity within physical media, such as water, atmospheres and the interior of astrophysical bodies. We outline the rather large body of research on the deformations of special relativity applicable within physical media, known under the name of isotopies . We then present, apparently for the first time, experimental verifications of the hypothesis formulated by the author in 1991, and today known as isoredshift , according to which light propagating within a physical medium experiences a shift of its frequency toward the red without any relative motion between the source, the medium and the observer, the shift originating from expected loss of energy to the medium due to interactions. We then confirm the isoredshift in the colors of our atmosphere as well as in the large difference in cosmological redshift between certain quasars and their associated galaxies; we indicate the consequential conceivable absence of universe expansion, big bang, dark matter, and dark energy; and propose systematic tests for the resolution of cosmological models via experiments on Earth along the teaching of Galileo Galilei .

Abstract
A friendly debate between the authors characterizes one that is prevalent among the community of ‘dissident’ physicists who do not accept Einstein’s relativity as the final explanation for the behavior of light. They wonder whether or not light acquires the velocity of its source. Maxwell’s equations strongly suggest a fixed speed for light upon its emission from a source. Is the emission point fixed in space? Would motion of the emitter alter the trajectory (and speed?) of the emitted light? Light’s immense speed makes determining this extremely difficult to answer on a scale less than astronomical. For example, despite supposed ‘definitive’ proof that there is no aether and light speed is universally constant alleged by proponents of a ‘null’ result from the 1887 Michelson-Morley Interferometer Experiment, debate continues over both of these subjects. The authors propose experiments using current technology that might be able to offer a definitive resolution to this debate, or possibly open up even more speculation.

Abstract
Electromagnetic waves (EMW) are formed by electric and magnetic fields, both together solution of Maxwell's equations. The reasoning they set out is standard: B is solenoidal always, E is solenoidal in charge-neutral regions, and this is conventionally taken to mean that both fields are perpendicular to the direction of propagation, with an electric scalar potential existing but no magnetic companion. Against this they claim two things for the same homogeneous case — that longitudinal magnetic fields are compatible with linearly polarised non-planar waves, and that magnetic scalar potentials are compatible with electromagnetic waves.

content_preview:
Extended Electromagnetic Theory: Space-Charge in Vacuo and the Rest Mass of the Photon
Book
Author Bo Lehnert , Sisir Roy
Language English

Subject Electromagnetism, photon physics
Published 1998
Publisher World Scientific Publishing Company
Pages 160
ISBN 9810233957
Extended Electromagnetic Theory: Space-Charge in Vacuo and the Rest Mass of the Photon is a 1998 monograph by Bo Lehnert and Sisir Roy , published by World Scientific (Contemporary Chemical Physics series, vol. 16).
Overview
The authors propose an extension of Maxwell's equations in which the divergence of the electric field and the electric conductivity in vacuo are allowed to be non-zero. From these modified equations they derive new features not present in conventional electromagnetism: both longitudinal and transverse wave solutions, a space-charge current in vacuo, and steady electromagnetic equilibria. Applications discussed include a model of the photon possessing a small non-zero rest mass and an axial magnetic-field component, and possible descriptions of charged and neutral leptons.
About the authors
Bo Lehnert is a Swedish plasma physicist and member of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, long associated with the Royal Institute of Technology (KTH), Stockholm. Sisir Roy is an Indian theoretical physicist (Indian Statistical Institute) working on the foundations of physics; see also his Statistical Geometry and Applications to Microphysics and Cosmology .

The EPEMC Gateway is an online portal and volunteer research community devoted to Extended Plasma-Electro-Magnetic Cosmology ( EPEMC ), a framework assembled by the American engineer and researcher Ramon Careaga . The site describes itself as "an open-source cosmology you can touch, interact with, critique, and test," and gathers papers, videos, primers, newsletters and links across plasma cosmology , the Electric Universe , electrical geology and meteorology, historic electrical science, and related subjects. The names PEM , PEMC , EPEMC and PEMS are described on the site as "open license trademarks of the community of the altstream."
The Gateway has been online in its present form since at least late 2021, and hosts a newsletter archive reaching back to 2017.
Framework
The Gateway distinguishes several layers of its own vocabulary:
PEM — plasma-electro-magnetic dynamics, the underlying physics of currents and fields in ionized matter.
PEMC — plasma-electro-magnetic cosmology, the application of that physics to the cosmos in the tradition of Hannes Alfvén , Winston H Bostick and Anthony L Peratt .
EPEMC — the "extended" programme, which carries the same physics into geology, meteorology, biology, medicine, archaeology, mythology and history.
MIMS — the "Membranous Interface of Material & Spiritual," a companion philosophical framework treating questions the site regards as lying outside empirical reach.

title: Extraction of Electrical Energy Directly from Space: The N-Machine
content_preview:
Title Extraction of Electrical Energy Directly from Space: The N-Machine
Read in full Link to paper
Author(s) Bruce E DePalma
Keywords Energy , Generator, Orgone, Prana, Od
Published 1979
No. of pages 9
Abstract
The extraction of energy directly from space has been suggested as a viable process for the solution of the energy problems of society. The accessibility of this energy has been limited by the necessity for the formulation of new energy paradigms. In the past, energy in space has been suggested by thoughts such as Orgone, Od, Prana, Bio-cosmic, Neutrino energy sea and so on, but the useful extraction of such energies has always awaited more explicit formulations of these ideas which could suggest the construction of simple practical energy extraction machinery.
Overview
Bruce E. DePalma proposes that electrical energy can be extracted directly from space by a rotating magnetised conductor, which he calls the N-machine, and presents the device as a generator that produces power without loading its drive.
The framing is an energy medium. DePalma writes that space is perfused with a "fine substance" lying between a space-time construct and gross matter, which confers inertia on objects and can be polarised. He lists earlier names for the same idea — Orgone, Od, Prana, bio-cosmic energy, the neutrino sea — and argues that what has been missing is a formulation explicit enough to suggest practical machinery.
His central physical claim is variable inertial mass. Experiments, he says, show that a rotating object's inertial mass becomes anisotropic: greater along the rotation axis and smaller in the plane of rotation, with complete polarisation when the in-plane inertial mass falls to zero at sufficient speed.

title: Extragalactic Evidence for Quantum Causality

Title Extragalactic Evidence for Quantum Causality
Read in full Link to paper
Author(s) Halton C Arp
Keywords nature of reality, quantum mechanics , Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen paradox
Published 1989
Journal Apeiron
Volume 1
Number 5
No. of pages 6
Pages 15-20
Abstract
In the conflict between Albert Einstein and Niels Bohr over the fundamental nature of reality, quantum mechanics was the experimental data being interpreted. The Copenhagen school maintained, crudely speaking, that reality at the microscopic level was to some extent subjective and acausal. Einstein, on the other hand, believed that no event was without cause and proposed the famous Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen paradox attacking the conclusions of quantum mechanics as being self-contradictory. The paradox, of course, was that quantum mechanics was observed to be experimentally true. The EPR proposal for an operational definition of reality was eminently sensible: If an event could be predicted with certainty it was real. The difficulty was that EPR did not discuss the aspect of locality. I would suggest extending their definition to read: To the extent that an event can be predicted it is locally causal; to the extent that an observed event is unpredictable it is real but only causal on a non-local scale.
Overview
Extragalactic Evidence for Quantum Causality is a six-page paper by Halton C Arp , written at the Max Planck Institut für Astrophysik in Garching and published in Apeiron number 5 (Fall 1989), pages 15–20 — the wiki record gives 7–9.
Arp was among the most accomplished observational astronomers of his generation, compiler of the Atlas of Peculiar Galaxies that still bears his name, and this paper connects his long-standing claims about anomalous redshifts to the Einstein–Bohr dispute over the nature of physical reality.
